subject.title: fix(qqbot): allow approval buttons in direct C2C conversations

question: Should unconfigured QQBot C2C fallback approvals remain limited to explicitly authorized command actors, or may the originating open-DM requester approve their own request when sender and conversation identity are securely bound end to end?
rationale: Current policy intentionally separates open-DM access from approval authority, while solving the reported timeout without explicit configuration requires choosing and enforcing a trusted direct approver identity.

options.title: Keep Explicit Approval Authority
options.body: Retain command/configured-approver authorization and improve the unauthorized direct-chat failure or setup guidance rather than treating every C2C sender as trusted.

options.title: Bind the Originating Requester
options.body: Add a durable approval-to-requester and conversation binding so only the sender who initiated that specific operation can resolve it.

options.title: Permit Every Direct Sender
options.body: Accept that any sender admitted by an open DM policy may resolve fallback approvals, explicitly owning the expanded security boundary.

recommendation.title: Keep Explicit Approval Authority
recommendation.body: Retain command/configured-approver authorization and improve the unauthorized direct-chat failure or setup guidance rather than treating every C2C sender as trusted.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior merged security hardening and its follow-up proof show the strongest ownership signal for this approval boundary.
